backlog.title: Documentation Drift Remediation (v2.9 chrome-disable aftermath)
backlog.description: Fix two documentation drift defects introduced by the v2.9 chrome-disable feature's documentation commits (b8f081d rewrote the providers.md table rows; 71e57c7a rewrote the how-it-works.md safety paragraph). Both are pure documentation edits — no source code, no manifest, no test logic changes. The chrome-disable feature itself is functionally correct and fully tested; only the surrounding prose the task re-touched was left stale.

milestones.title: Fix both identified documentation inconsistencies
milestones.description: Correct the opencode Delivery value in docs/providers.md (Major Issue 1) and complete the provider enumeration in the docs/how-it-works.md safety paragraph (Minor Issue 2). Then perform a final cross-doc consistency sweep to verify no other drift remains.

tasks.title: Fix opencode Delivery column drift in docs/providers.md
tasks.description: The opencode row in the 7-provider table reports `positional` for Delivery, but the shipped binary, builtin.go, builtin_test.go decode-parity TOML, and providers/opencode.toml all agree the value is `stdin`. This drift was introduced when commit b8f081d rewrote the table row to add the Chrome-disable column and carried the stale PRD §12.6 value forward. Fix the single table cell to restore byte-faithfulness with the binary.

subtasks.title: Correct opencode row Delivery cell from 'positional' to 'stdin' in docs/providers.md
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/016_e6bf7715e06e/bugfix/001_19019b487eea/architecture/system_context.md §Defect 1 for the full binary cross-check and root-cause git-blame trace. The opencode row is line 82 of docs/providers.md. The Delivery column is the 2nd column in the markdown table (column order: Provider, Delivery, Print flag, Model flag, Default model, System prompt flag, Tool-disable approach, Chrome-disable, Stager?). The current cell text is the literal word `positional`; it must become the literal word `stdin`.
2. INPUT: The authoritative value is `stdin`, confirmed from FOUR independent sources: (a) binary — `stagecoach providers show opencode` prints `prompt_delivery = 'stdin'`; (b) source — internal/provider/builtin.go line 327 `PromptDelivery: strPtr("stdin")` inside builtinOpenCode(); (c) reference TOML — providers/opencode.toml line 45 `prompt_delivery = "stdin"`; (d) test TOML — internal/provider/builtin_test.go line 87 decode-parity block. No other column in the opencode row changes. No other table row changes (all 6 other providers already match the binary — verified 2026-07-13).
3. LOGIC: In docs/providers.md, locate line 82 (the `| \`opencode\` |` table row). Change the Delivery cell from `positional` to `stdin`. Do NOT alter any other cell in that row, any other row, the table header, or any prose elsewhere in the file. The file's own "Rendered command" guidance and the providers/opencode.toml RENDERED COMMAND header already correctly show stdin piping (`< "<sys>\n\n<user payload>"`), so no cascade edits are needed.
4. OUTPUT: docs/providers.md with line 82's opencode Delivery cell reading `stdin`. After the change, all 7 provider rows in the table must have Delivery values matching their binary `prompt_delivery` (pi=stdin, claude=stdin, opencode=stdin, codex=stdin, cursor=positional, agy=stdin, qwen-code=stdin). The file must remain valid markdown with consistent table column alignment.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] This IS a documentation file edit — the fix is the doc update. No separate docs subtask needed. Verify no other doc file references the opencode delivery method as 'positional' (check README.md, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/README.md — none should need changes based on prior research, but verify).

tasks.title: Fix safety paragraph provider enumeration in docs/how-it-works.md
tasks.description: The '### Safety invariant' paragraph (line 197) makes a universal claim ('Every built-in manifest constrains the agent to a read-only mode') but names only 4 of 7 providers in its two-category partition. The read-only-constraint category should contain 5 providers (codex, cursor, agy, qwen-code, opencode) per the same file's provider table and the docs/providers.md Chrome-disable column. Fix the parenthetical to be either exhaustive or explicitly exemplary.

subtasks.title: Expand read-only constraint flags parenthetical to cover all 5 constrained providers
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/016_e6bf7715e06e/bugfix/001_19019b487eea/architecture/system_context.md §Defect 2 for the full analysis. The paragraph is line 197 of docs/how-it-works.md. The current text reads: '… either via explicit tool-disable flags (pi, claude) or read-only constraint flags (codex, cursor). …' — only 4 of 7 providers are named. The 3 omitted providers (agy, qwen-code, opencode) ARE read-only-constrained (agy via --mode plan; qwen-code via --approval-mode default; opencode's `run` subcommand is read-only by design). The sentence starts with 'Every built-in manifest' — a universal claim that implies exhaustiveness.
2. INPUT: The 5 read-only-constrained providers and their mechanisms (verified against internal/provider/builtin.go bare_flags and docs/providers.md Tool-disable approach column): codex (--sandbox read-only --ephemeral), cursor (--mode ask --trust), agy (--mode plan), qwen-code (--approval-mode default), opencode (run subcommand, read-only by design). The 2 explicit-switch providers (pi, claude) are correctly named and need no change.
3. LOGIC: In docs/how-it-works.md line 197, replace the parenthetical `(codex, cursor)` with an expanded form. Two acceptable options (the PRD §Issue 2 Suggested Fix offers both):
   - PREFERRED (exhaustive): `read-only constraint flags (codex, cursor, agy, qwen-code; opencode's \`run\` is read-only by design)` — matches the universal 'Every' claim and lists all 5.
   - ALTERNATIVE (exemplary): `read-only constraint flags (e.g. codex, cursor)` — smaller change, but slightly weakens precision.
   Use the exhaustive form unless it makes the sentence unwieldy. Do NOT change the 'explicit tool-disable flags (pi, claude)' parenthetical — it is correct (pi and claude are the only two explicit-switch providers). Do NOT change any other sentence in the paragraph. The remainder of the paragraph (chrome-less sentence, cross-reference link) stays untouched.
4. OUTPUT: docs/how-it-works.md line 197 with the read-only constraint flags parenthetical naming all 5 constrained providers (or using 'e.g.'). The sentence must read naturally and accurately. The provider list must be consistent with docs/providers.md's Tool-disable approach column and the Chrome-disable column.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] This IS a documentation file edit — the fix is the doc update. No separate docs subtask needed.
